10.2139/ssrn.7404325.abstract: Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction (NO₃RR) offers a promising route for ammonia synthesis, but is hindered by slow kinetics and competitive hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Herein, ultrathin Cu‐doped Co₃O₄/reduced graphene oxide (Cu‐Co₃O₄/rGO) nanosheets are prepared through the morphology and electronic structure modulation for efficient NO₃RR performance. Combined experiments and DFT computations disclose that Cu doping induces 2D nanosheet morphology, up-modulates the d‐band center to optimize the adsorption strengthen of reactants and key intermediates, and constructs Cu‐Co tandem sites for cascade catalysis, while rGO improves the composite conductivity. The optimized catalyst exhibits a Faradaic efficiency of 98.5% at -0.7 V vs. RHE and an ammonia yield of 25.2 mg h-¹ mgcat-¹ at -1.0 V vs. RHE with high stability. The in‐situ electro‐generated ammonia acts directly as a base catalyst for chalcone synthesis with 75.9% conversion, constructing a waste‐to‐resource‐to‐value model integrating nitrate remediation and sustainable fine‐chemical synthesis.

10.2139/ssrn.7422403.abstract: Ammonia decomposition catalysts for hydrogen release have attracted increasing attention as a key technology for achieving a carbon-neutral society. In this study, we systematically investigated the enhancement of catalytic activity and synergistic effects in ammonia decomposition by introducing alkali metal promoters, cesium (Cs) and potassium (K), individually and in combination, into Ru/CeO2 catalysts. The Ru/CeO2 catalyst co-promoted with Cs and K exhibited significantly higher ammonia conversion and turnover frequency (TOF = 0.936 s-1) than catalysts containing a single promoter or no promoter. Notably, approximately 90% ammonia conversion and excellent long-term stability were achieved at 450 ℃. In particular, the K-Cs-Ru/CeO2 catalyst showed the highest electron density at the Ru active sites, enhanced metal–support interactions, and the greatest concentration of oxygen vacancies, which were associated with an increased Ce3+ ratio. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations revealed that promoter-induced modulation of the electronic structure of Ru d orbitals and Ru-N interactions in Ru/CeO2-based catalysts can enhance ammonia decomposition activity. These combined experimental and theoretical results provide valuable insights into the rational design of high-performance catalysts for ammonia-based hydrogen production and establish an important foundation for the development of low-temperature, high-efficiency ammonia decomposition processes.

10.2139/ssrn.7422743.abstract: Electrocatalytic ammonia oxidation reaction (EAOR) offers a promising route for ammonia-nitrogen removal and energy-saving hydrogen production, yet its practical application is still limited by the sluggish reaction kinetics of non-noble-metal catalysts. Herein, a heating-rate-regulated defect-engineering strategy is proposed to construct oxygen-vacancy-rich MOF-derived NiCu oxide electrocatalysts. A bimetallic NiCu-NH2-BDC MOF precursor was thermally converted into NiCu oxide electrodes at heating rates of 1, 5, and 10 °C min-1. The optimized M-NiCuOx-1°C with a nanosheet-derived porous architecture exhibits superior EAOR performance, requiring only 397 and 516 mV to reach 50 and 100 mA cm-2, respectively, with a low Tafel slope of 23.2 mV dec-1. Post-reaction XPS reveals substantial NiOOH-like surface reconstruction, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations further demonstrate that Cu incorporation into NiOOH lowers the key intermediate-stage dehydrogenation barrier from 1.03 to 0.82 eV. In a two-chamber reactor, M-NiCuOx-1°C achieves 98.1% ammonia-nitrogen removal within 5 h and presents good stability. This work highlights heating-rate-controlled oxygen-vacancy engineering as an effective strategy for designing MOF-derived catalysts for efficient EAOR.

10.2139/ssrn.7439064.abstract: Removing carbon dioxide (CO₂) from syngas is necessary in ammonia production since the presence of CO₂ can cause poisoning of the downstream catalysts, formation of carbamates/carbondates and can add to the operation challenges. Three chemical solvents (monoethanolamine (MEA), diethanolamine (DEA) and methyldiethanolamine (MDEA)) are compared with diethylene glycol dimethyl ether (DEGDME) in this study for simulating the absorption of CO₂ from high pressure syngas from an ammonia plant. 277,792 kg/hr of sour syngas (17.34 mol% CO₂) was contacted counter-currently with 3591 m³/hr of lean solvent (50 wt% solvent) in a five-tray absorber at 70 °C and 3628 kPa and 48.3 °C and 4114 kPa, respectively. The CO₂ removal performance was compared by carrying out tray-by-tray analysis which indicated that MEA performed best due to the fast rate of carbamate formation, decreasing the CO₂ composition in the vapour phase from 0.1734 to 0.0010 mol/mol. DEA was able to achieve a moderate removal of CO₂ (0.0774) and DEGDME reduced CO₂ by physical solubility (0.0915). MDEA had the poorest performance, with CO₂ 0.1331. These absorption trends were supported by the corresponding solvent flows, which had the highest increase in loading for MEA. The results show the sequence of reactivity of primary amines, secondary amines, and tertiary amines as well as confirm that stage-wise simulation is an effective screening method for investigating CO₂-removal solvents prior to pilot-scale testing.

10.2139/ssrn.7445994.abstract: In a world committed to reducing CO2 emissions, alternative fuels such as SAF and methanol are expected to gain importance to decarbonize hard-to-abate sectors. As an alternative to the development of direct CO2 to fuels conversion processes, green syngas production can be a practical approach to accomplish this target. Reverse Water Gas Shift performed in electrified reactors represents a flexible technology, enabling the production of CO from CO2 and green hydrogen and, in turns, the application of the several available routes of the syngas platform to liquid energy and hydrogen carriers. Given the endothermic nature of the reaction and the thermodynamic requirements, high temperature heating by electrification is an open challenge. With this work we provide a detailed thermal characterization of a directly electrified SiSiC packed foam reactor loaded with Rh-based catalyst used for CO2 utilization via Reverse Water Gas Shift. The system was operated up to 5 bar, 18 Nm3/kgcat/h and 750°C achieving equilibrium CO2 conversion and CO-selectivity. Measured axial temperature profiles showed a sharp temperature increase at the inlet of the catalytic bed which was emphasized when increasing the operating pressure. This trend was attributed to the exothermicity of methanation which competes with RWGS at low temperatures and high pressures. Such interpretations were corroborated by simulation results obtained with a 2D mathematical model of the reactor which could accurately describe the observed reactor behaviour: simulated composition axial profiles confirmed in fact a substantial production of methane in the first portion of the packed foam which translated into a temperature increase.

10.2139/ssrn.7471149.abstract: Nitrogen (N2) activation and active hydrogen (*H) supply represent the major challenges in the ammonia (NH3) synthesis process nowadays. In this work, FeVO4 photocatalysts with abundant oxygen vacancies (FeVO4-OV) were prepared by a one-step hydrothermal combined with secondary annealing method. Following optimization, the FeVO4 catalyst exhibited a substantially enhanced photocatalytic ammonia synthesis rate of 43.71 μmol⋅h-1⋅g-1, surpassing that of the pristine sample by a factor of 3.4. Experimental characterizations, combined with density-functional theory (DFT) calculations, confirmed that the nitrogen reduction of FeVO4-OV proceeds via an alternating pathway, with the active center of reduction being the V site adjacent to the marginal oxygen vacancies (OVs). The valence transition of V4+/V5+ and the synergistic effect with OVs are the exact centers of activity for the photocatalytic nitrogen reduction reaction (PNRR) with FeVO4. The sustained and efficient valence transition and electron transfer of V4+/V5+ in the presence of OVs facilitates the N2 reduction reaction process. Furthermore, under the influence of OVs, Fe sites promote water dissociation to supply *H, which plays a pivotal role in the PNRR process. The synergistic effect combined with the dual sites and OVs enhances the performance of PNRR with FeVO4-based catalysts. This work establishes a rational framework for designing efficient and environmentally benign photocatalysts for nitrogen reduction.

10.2139/ssrn.7506406.abstract: Catalyst geometry strongly influences transport and reaction in ammonia decomposition reactors, but its relative performance can change upon reactor scale-up. A multiscale computational fluid dynamics (CFD) framework was therefore employed to investigate catalyst geometry effects from particle resolved to reactor scales. Unlike conventional porous medium approaches, the present model explicitly resolves catalyst packing structures generated using Blender based rigid body packing simulations. Kinetic parameters of the Temkin–Pyzhev ammonia decomposition model were estimated from experimental data using a one-dimensional (1D) gPROMS model and implemented into ANSYS Fluent through a user defined function (UDF). The particle resolved CFD results were subsequently extended to two scale-up reactor models using catalyst geometry dependent parameters to evaluate the effects of catalyst shape on ammonia decomposition performance.,Particle resolved CFD simulations showed that the sphere catalyst achieved the highest ammonia conversion of approximately 86%, whereas the 7-hole and 1-hole catalysts exhibited lower conversions of approximately 75% and 66%, respectively, despite their larger surface to volume ratios. In contrast, the scale-up simulations showed that the 7-hole catalyst achieved the highest conversion of 48.47% in the double-tube reactor, where enhanced reactor level heat transfer enabled more effective utilization of its enlarged reaction surface. This reversal demonstrates that the relative performance of different catalyst geometries can change upon scale-up as the contribution of reactor-scale heat transfer becomes increasingly important. These findings highlight that catalyst performance is governed by the coupling between reaction surface area and its thermal and hydrodynamic accessibility, emphasizing the need to consider catalyst geometry and reactor configuration together.

10.2139/ssrn.7540840.abstract: Spatially selective phase transformation remains difficult to control in Ti₂AlNb-based alloys because grain boundaries and multiphase interfaces experience different thermal and diffusional conditions. Thus, a tailored multi-pass electropulsing treatment process was applied to Ti–22Al–26Nb alloy. Results show that the first-stage treatment reduced the average α₂ particle size from 3.15 to 2.15 μm and produced an approximately 4.22 mm-long α₂-enriched band. Subsequent EPT triggered a unique heterogeneous structure characterized by a size gradient from the grain boundary toward the grain interior and a characteristic unit consisting of three O lamella with mutual geometric misorientations of 60° which share a common <012> direction through coupled local joule heating and solute redistribution. Nanoscale acicular O precipitated within Nb-enriched rim O and evolved toward lamella, indicating a rim O→secondary O decomposition pathway. Finally, high UTS of 1208.6 MPa was achieved. Sequential electropulsing therefore enables therefore enables coordinated control of selective phase decomposition, precipitation and variant reconfiguration.

10.2139/ssrn.7566340.abstract: Although catalytic wet peroxide oxidation (CWPO) effectively remediates organic wastewater, high reagent requirements and slow reaction kinetics limit its practical application. Here, a core-shell Fe3O4@ZIF‒67 catalyst (FOZIF) was synthesized and used in an induction heating-assisted CWPO (IH‒CWPO) system for the rapid and efficient generation of reactive radicals. In this system, induction heating synergistically accelerates H2O2 activation over the FOZIF catalyst to generate abundant hydroxyl radicals. Mechanistically, the electron-donating Fe2+ species in the Fe3O4 core accelerate the Co3+/Co2+ redox cycle within the ZIF-67 shell, establishing a dual Fe/Co active site network. Consequently, the optimized FOZIF‒2 catalyst achieved 98.2% degradation of tetracycline (TC) within 30 min in the IH‒CWPO system, yielding a remarkable rate constant of 1.46 × 10−1 min−1, significantly outperforming conventional CWPO. After four cycles of operation, the TC removal efficiency dropped by only ~16%, confirming the good magnetic recyclability and operational stability of FOZIF‒2 in the IH‒CWPO system. This research highlights the promise of combining electromagnetic heating with MOF-based magnetic catalysts for highly efficient wastewater treatment.

10.2139/ssrn.7571359.abstract: The low electronic conductivity of TiO2 limits its rate capability as a lithium-ion battery anode. 10.2139/ssrn.7576410.abstract: Carbon-based materials attenuate strongly yet suffer from impedance mismatch due to an excessive dielectric response, limiting the lightweight, thin, and broadband absorbers required for electromagnetic protection. Here, graphene sheets were assembled into a nitrogen-doped three-dimensional graphene framework (N-3DG), and the in situ confined growth of high-entropy alloy (FeCoNiCrMn) nanoparticles was achieved via flash Joule heating. The alloy components moderate the excessive dielectric response of the N-3DG framework, allowing incident electromagnetic waves to enter the absorber effectively. Meanwhile, alloy compositional evolution enhances polarization loss and synergistically improves impedance matching and attenuation. The optimized N-3DG/FeCoNiCrMn composite achieves a minimum reflection loss of -62.49 dB at 11.92 GHz with a thickness of 2.06 mm at a filler loading of only 15 wt%, together with an effective absorption bandwidth of at least 5.36 GHz (12.64-18 GHz) at 1.69 mm, whereas pristine N-3DG shows no effective absorption band (RL ≤ -10 dB) over 2-18 GHz. 10.2139/ssrn.7593750.abstract: Direct ammonia fuel cells offer a carbon-free pathway for electrochemical energy conversion. Nevertheless, the anodic ammonia oxidation reaction (AOR) involves multistep dehydrogenation, N–N bond formation, and complex intermediate evolution, giving rise to substantial kinetic and thermodynamic challenges. Herein, density functional theory calculations are employed to probe the central-metal effect of graphene-supported Fe–N4, Co–N4, and Ni–N4 single-atom sites with identical first coordination shells. Formation-energy calculations and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations indicate favorable metal anchoring and finite-temperature structural persistence for all three models. Bader charge analysis reveals metal-to-coordination-environment charge transfers of 1.26, 1.07, and 0.96 e for Fe, Co, and Ni, respectively. After NH3 adsorption, the N–TM distances are 2.31, 2.20, and 2.95 Å, alongside net interfacial charge transfers of approximately 0.18, 0.10, and 0.01 e. Free-energy analysis of three competing AOR pathways demonstrates that N–N coupling at the *NH2 intermediate stage (Path I) is thermodynamically favored over further dehydrogenation across all three active sites. The maximum uphill free-energy variations along Path I reach 1.44, 0.99, and 1.76 eV for Fe–N4, Co–N4, and Ni–N4, respectively, yielding limiting potentials of −1.44, −0.99, and −1.76 V. The favorable AOR thermodynamics of Co–N4 are associated with balanced interfacial coupling, a reduced thermodynamic penalty for generating the N–N-coupled intermediate, and nearly thermoneutral N2 release.These findings demonstrate that desirable AOR thermodynamics are determined by balanced intermediate stabilization, instead of merely maximizing charge-transfer magnitude or adsorption strength.

10.2139/ssrn.7606957.abstract: Bismuth-based alloy anodes offer high sodium-storage capacity but suffer from structural and kinetic limitations associated with repeated alloying/dealloying. Herein, Bi-containing coal tar pitch-derived carbon nanofibers (CTP-TU-Bi) were prepared by electrospinning, pre-oxidation, and Joule heating and directly used as flexible binder-free anodes for sodium-ion batteries. Joule heating was used to convert the electrospun precursor into a continuous carbon nanofiber framework containing crystalline Bi nanoparticles. Microscopy and XPS results support the formation of Bi-C interfaces and changes in the local chemical environment. Density functional theory calculations based on simplified carbon and Bi-containing models indicate more favorable Na adsorption and a lower calculated Na migration barrier in the Bi-containing model. The optimized CTP-TU-Bi-0.6 electrode delivers 301.8 mAh g-1 at 0.03 A g-1 (0.1C) and retains 170 mAh g-1 after 350 cycles at 0.1 C, while 81.48 mAh g-1 is retained after 1200 cycles at 0.6 A g-1 (2 C). These results indicate that the integration of Bi nanoparticles with the carbon nanofiber framework and the associated Bi-C interfacial characteristics contribute to the improved sodium-storage performance.

10.2139/ssrn.7624667.abstract: AbstractThis paper proposes an integrated energy-system architecture in which flexible industrial demand is used as an additional resource for balancing nuclear and renewable electricity generation. The proposed framework is based on four principles: continuous operation of nuclear generation according to an “Always On” principle; grid-first operation; maximized integration of renewable generation subject to system requirements; and redirection of surplus or otherwise constrained electricity to flexible industrial production rather than relying primarily on generation curtailment.Green ammonia and green methane are considered two complementary Power-to-X pathways for converting available electricity into value-added products and chemical energy carriers. The proposed architecture integrates electrolysis, hydrogen management, ammonia synthesis, methane production, and a Central Energy Management System (CEMS) capable of coordinating electricity availability, industrial demand, production processes, and grid requirements. Flexible production is therefore treated not simply as electricity consumption, but as a controllable demand-side resource that can respond to changes in the power-system balance.The paper discusses the technical configuration, flexibility mechanism, energy-management architecture, and economic rationale of the proposed approach and compares its functional characteristics with conventional pumped-storage balancing. Ukraine is used as an illustrative country case because of its combination of nuclear generation, renewable-energy potential, existing industrial infrastructure, and demand for low-carbon chemical products and fertilizers. The proposed framework provides a pathway from power generation to value generation by integrating energy-system balancing with industrial production.

10.2139/ssrn.7629221.abstract: Ammonia co-firing reduces direct CO₂ emissions from coal-fired plants but changes furnace heat transfer, flue-gas losses, and steam-temperature control. This study evaluates a 1,000 MW-class ultra-supercritical once-through coal-fired plant at ammonia energy fractions of 0–100%, with fuel allocation and efficiency calculated using lower heating values (LHVs) at 25°C. Degradation is decomposed into composition and temperature contributions, and ammonia preheating and tuning are assessed within a common plant boundary. At 100% ammonia, net efficiency decreases by 1.22 percentage points (pp) on an LHV basis and 6.24 pp on a higher heating value (HHV) basis relative to coal. First-stage preheating (PH1), controlled to recover the additional sensible exhaust heat caused by the higher flue-gas temperature, restores 59–98% of the temperature-related net-efficiency loss at 20%, 50%, and 100% ammonia under rated-load conditions. Recovery reaches 0.78 pp at 100% ammonia. Second-stage preheating with extraction steam adds 0.23 pp because the boiler gain exceeds the cycle penalty. Combining preheating and tuning restores 1.33 pp and reduces fuel consumption per unit net electricity by 3.02%, while maintaining a spray ratio near 7% at rated load. Preheating and air adjustment improve efficiency, whereas separator outlet enthalpy adjustment restores spray control margin. At subcritical part load, the outlet-superheat requirement restricts this adjustment; at 75% load and 100% ammonia, combined-case spray stays within capacity but reaches about 21% of main-steam flow, above the 14% design ratio. The results link loss decomposition to heat-recovery design; combustion, emission, and equipment constraints require further validation.

10.2139/ssrn.7674319.abstract: ABSTRACT: Electrochemical nitrate reduction to ammonia (NO3-RR) enables nitrate removal from contaminated water together with decentralized ammonia production. However, in the near-neutral media commonly encountered in nitrate-containing wastewater, sluggish water dissociation and limited interfacial proton availability severely constrain the reaction kinetics and ammonia production efficiency. To address this challenge, we constructed a Pd-Cu2O metal-metal oxide catalyst featuring synergistic dual active sites (Pd3Cu1/NF). Experimental results demonstrate that the synergistic coupling between Pd and Cu sites regulates interfacial water adsorption and hydrogen-bonding configurations, promotes water activation and the generation and transfer of reactive hydrogen species, and thereby accelerates the consecutive hydrogenation and deoxygenation of nitrate to ammonia. Benefiting from these synergistic effects, Pd3Cu1/NF delivers excellent NO3-RR performance in a near-neutral electrolyte, achieving a Faradaic efficiency of 92% and an ammonia yield rate of 1.36 mmol cm-2 h-1 at -1.2 V versus RHE, which is 2.72 times that of Cu/NF. The catalyst also maintains stable performance over 40 consecutive cycles. This work establishes a broadly applicable metal-metal oxide catalyst design strategy for efficient electrochemical nitrate-to-ammonia conversion under mild conditions through the regulation and effective utilization of interfacial proton supply.

10.2298/tsci260121096y.abstract: In this study, A three-dimensional multiphysics model coupling electric and thermal fields was developed to systematically explore the effects of microscopic structural parameters (wire diameter and spacing) on current density distribution, Joule heat source characteristics, and temperature field uniformity within the Joule heating catalyst support (JHCS).The results indicated that increasing the wire diameter directed current shunt toward the branch channels, thereby improving heat generation uniformity. Conversely, increasing the wire spacing led to current "dead zones" in the branch channels due to increased electrical resistance. This non-uniformity was further amplified because Joule heat was proportional to the square of the current density. The temperature field was primarily governed by the heat transfer radius determined by the pore size of the JHCS; excessively small wire diameters or large spacings resulted in significant low-temperature zones at the channel centers. Synthetically, a wire diameter of 0.10 mm and a wire spacing of 0.25 mm were identified as the optimal structure, achieving a balance between heat generation efficiency and thermal uniformity.
